title: Feasibility of running the ET-SoC-1 without its heatsink
description: Whether an ET-SoC-1 card can run with its heatsink off so that a sensor can look straight at the chip, worked out from the cards' measured leakage laws, the fitted heatsink model and a Monte Carlo model of the bare package, and checked against vendor θJA tables, published bare-processor runs and infrared-window cooler studies: in the model a bare 600 MHz card almost never holds a stable temperature (1 of 3,600 draws), and a sensor would see a plated lid at nearly one temperature. A thermocouple taped to the heatsink base, heatsink on and never between lid and heatsink, is safe with the card off; one soldered into a groove in the lid needs the lab's consent and carries moderate risk. Either belongs on the visit the lab-problems page already requests.
